question.title: Amendment No. 1: Limitation On Assessment Of Real Property Used For Residential Purposes

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, Initiatives / Amendments / Revisions Database, detail page "Limitation on Assessment of Real Property Used for Residential Purposes"

ballot_text.source_title: Ballot Number 1, Election Year 2022: Limitation on Assessment of Real Property Used for Residential Purposes
ballot_text.type_quote: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution, effective January 1, 2023

fact.quote: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution, effective January 1, 2023, to authorize the Legislature, by general law, to prohibit the consideration of any change or improvement made to real property used for residential purposes
fact.why: HJR 1377 lets the Legislature exclude flood-resistance improvements from assessed value for ad valorem taxation, which lowers assessments. The full text was read and contains no provision that imposes, authorizes or sets any tax or fee. Inferred.

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, Initiatives / Amendments / Revisions Database, detail page "Limitation on Assessment of Real Property Used for Residential Purposes"

threshold.rule: at least 60% of the electors voting on the measure
threshold.quote: Unless otherwise specifically provided for elsewhere in this constitution, if the proposed amendment or revision is approved by vote of at least sixty percent of the electors voting on the measure, it shall be effective as an amendment to or revision of the constitution
threshold.matched: by the type the source's title states (amendment); the ballot text shows it is not an amendment that imposes a new State tax or fee [inferred] (data/measure/ballot-texts.json)

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures
p.note: this route's back-test of statewide measures shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (11 against 6.8 within 1 point of ½, and 10 against 6.2 within 20,000 votes, 2018 to 2024), so p may be low

question.title: Amendment No. 2: Abolishing The Constitution Revision Commission

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, Initiatives / Amendments / Revisions Database, detail page "Abolishing the Constitution Revision Commission"

ballot_text.source_title: Ballot Number 2, Election Year 2022: Abolishing the Constitution Revision Commission
ballot_text.type_quote: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution to abolish the Constitution Revision Commission

fact.quote: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution to abolish the Constitution Revision Commission, which meets at 20-year intervals and is scheduled to next convene in 2037
fact.why: SJR 204 abolishes a commission; the only tax words in its text are the name of the Taxation and Budget Reform Commission, which it leaves in place. No tax or fee is imposed. Inferred.
